Iris (AM): Heads-up — Meridian Finance wants to convert the POC to a 12‑month enterprise commit. Asks: reserved GPUs for steady latency, autoscale/burst runway for earnings reports, hard monthly burst cap, and written KMS + audit answers for procurement.

Dmitri (SE): Do we have their traffic shape? sustained qps, burst peaks, token sizes? Need this to size reserved pool and burst runway.

Iris (AM): Customer sketch: steady 180 qps daytime, nightly batch embeddings (parallel 120 jobs), two predictable earnings spikes/day to ~3k qps lasting 90–180s. Avg chat tokens ~130 in / 110 out. Targets: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 450ms. Finance wants committed cost vs burst worst-case.

Harper (SRE): Quick conservative perf numbers from our bench (decoder int8): assume 45 qps/GPU at p95 for ~240 token seq w/o heavy batching. With KV cache + light batching you can reach ~80 qps/GPU. Use conservative 45 qps for commit math.

Dmitri (SE): Baseline 180 -> 4 GPUs (180/45 = 4). Burst delta = 3000-180 = 2820 qps. If same model -> ~63 GPUs. But realistic plan: reserved 4 + burst runway using quantized "burst" replicas at ~120 qps/GPU and aggressive batching. That gives ~24 GPUs for peak. Recommend offering burst credits to cover N minutes at discounted burst rate + tenant hard cap option.

Harper (SRE): Operational notes: preheat KV/cache 10–15min before scheduled spikes; cross-AZ spread for eviction tolerance; spot fallback for non-SLA capacity. Short warm command we use in staging:

./warm --qps 1500 --concurrency 200 --seq 240 --duration 120

Also implement a degradation ladder: full model -> quantized model -> shorter outputs -> deny non-critical batch jobs when cap hit. Document expected SLOs per step.

Noel (Sales Eng): Pricing shapes: (A) Committed: 4 reserved GPUs + monthly platform fee + 12mo discount (show per-token equivalent). (B) Committed + burst credits: pre-purchase X GPU-minutes/month at discounted rate with optional hard cap. (C) Private VPC/on-prem: adds license + integration fee. Include sample invoice numbers.

Iris (AM): Security asks: CMK for data at rest, 1y audit retention + SIEM export, SOC2 evidence, and whether private VPC reduces procurement friction for PHI/PCI style data.

Harper (SRE): We support customer-managed keys via KMS, audit log export to SIEM, and private VPC deployments. On-prem option exists but increases integration time and fees. I'll attach the infra checklist for CMK + log forwarding.

Dmitri (SE): Action items: I'll produce a 1‑pager capacity calc with assumptions and GPU counts + cost worksheet. Harper will add the preheat/runbook + security checklist. Noel will draft pricing slides + contract language for burst credits and hard cap. Iris will gather procurement contacts and legal asks.

infra-bot: Created ticket POC-12234 "Meridian Finance commit: reserve 4 GPUs + burst runway + CMK & audit answers" assigned to @Dmitri @Harper @Noel.

Iris (AM): Can we meet in 40m to finalize before sending procurement pack?

Dmitri (SE): Yes, ping me.

Harper (SRE): Available.

Noel (Sales Eng): On it.
